headline: 1,314 hospitalised as 4 more die of dengue in 24 hours
summary: The total death toll has risen to 121, with 43,904 cases recorded across Bangladesh, according to the DGHS.
details: At least four dengue patients died and 1,314 others were hospitalised in the last 24 hours, according to the Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS).
Of the latest deaths, two were reported in the Khulna division, while Dhaka South City Corporation and the Dhaka division reported one death each.
With these new additions, the total number of dengue deaths in the country has risen to 121.
The total number of recorded dengue cases has now reached 43,904.
Currently, 3,074 dengue patients are undergoing treatment at hospitals across the country.

headline: August inflation eases to 8.26%, down from July
summary: Food inflation fell to 7.02%, providing some relief to consumers, though non-food inflation saw a slight increase.
details: Inflation in Bangladesh eased slightly to 8.26 percent in August, down from 8.32 percent in July, according to data from the Bangladesh Bureau of Statistics (BBS).
The decline was driven by a slower rate of increase in food prices, with food inflation falling to 7.02 percent in August compared to 7.16 percent in July.
However, this was partly offset by a rise in non-food inflation, which increased from 9.28 percent to 9.32 percent during the same period.
On a month-to-month basis, the general price index rose 2.31 percent in August, while the rate for food items increased by 3.86 percent.
This indicates that while annual inflation eased marginally, prices continued to rise sequentially, with food items showing a higher monthly increase.
caption:
Inflation dipped slightly to 8.26% in August. Is your monthly budget feeling the relief?

Inflation in Bangladesh eased slightly to 8.26 percent in August, down from 8.32 percent in July, according to data from the Bangladesh Bureau of Statistics (BBS).

The decline was driven by a slower rate of increase in food prices, with food inflation falling to 7.02 percent in August compared to 7.16 percent in July.

However, this was partly offset by a rise in non-food inflation, which increased from 9.28 percent to 9.32 percent during the same period.

On a month-to-month basis, the general price index rose 2.31 percent in August, while the rate for food items increased by 3.86 percent.

This indicates that while annual inflation eased marginally, prices continued to rise sequentially, with food items showing a higher monthly increase.

#Bangladesh #Inflation #Economy #BBS #PriceHike

Source: Prothom Alo, The Daily Star
